description: Every command a page may call on the shell that hosts it, as window.bridge.call(name, args), and every event the shell may send the page, as window.bridge.on(name, handler). Each shell implements exactly these and refuses anything else (desktop/test/bridge.test.js). A platform difference is data here, never a branch in core.

app.icon.note: The app icon chosen in Settings (appearance.appIcon, issue 167), one of the ids core/spec/app-icons.json names. Each shell applies it where its platform can and answers { applied, icon }: the desktop sets its window's and Dock's icon, iOS sets the alternate icon set AppIcon-<id> (the default is the primary icon), Android enables the launcher alias .AppIcon_<id> and disables the others. An id the spec does not name is refused with applied false.

link.take.note: The messaging link (sms:, smsto:, mms:, mmsto:, im:, imessage:) the platform last handed this app as its default for messages (issue 333), answered once and then forgotten. The page asks when it is ready, whenever it is shown, and on app.link, and parses the link itself (core/app/rules/chats.js parseMessagingLink).

notify.note: A message notice carries the conversation and the message it announced (issue 331), so a press on it opens that conversation at that message. The shell keeps the pair with the notice and hands it back through notify.take when the notice is pressed.

notify.take.note: The notice the person last pressed, as { chatId, messageId }, or null; taking it clears it, so one press opens one message (issue 331). A shell raises notify.opened when a notice is pressed, and the page takes it then and again once it has signed in, so a press that launched the app is answered too.

notify.permission.note: Notifications are asked for once the person has signed in (issue 327), not on the first message: with request true a shell that has not been answered asks the system, and every shell answers where it stands, one of granted, denied, requested (asked, the answer still coming) or unsupported.

file.save.note: A document pressed in a conversation (issue 219) is offered for saving under its real name: the page hands the shell the file's bytes as base64 with that name and type. The desktop opens a save dialog, and a phone opens its system share or save sheet, which includes Save to Files. A shell that cannot save answers false.

icon.redraw.note: The app icon follows the active theme (issue 189): the page sends the scheme it draws, the colour tokens the icon reads (core/app/rules/icon.js ICON_TOKENS) as it resolved them, and the total unread count. The desktop redraws its tray image, its window icon and the Windows taskbar overlay from them and sets the count the Dock and Linux launchers draw, answering true; a phone cannot recolour its icon at runtime and answers false.

app.link.note: A messaging link has arrived; the page takes it with link.take. The iPhone has no event stream, so there the page asks when it is shown.

notify.opened.note: A notice was pressed (issue 331): the page takes it with notify.take. The event carries nothing, so the one held press is the only answer and a page that was not listening yet still finds it.
